newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says will not nag U.S. to deliver on NAFTA.
newsitem.headline: Chile says will not nag U.S. to deliver on NAFTA.

text.p: Chile will not nag the United States to deliver on its promise to bring the country into NAFTA when President Eduardo Frei visits the White House next month, Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said on Wednesday.
Insulza said Frei and President Bill Clinton would discuss Chile's wish to join NAFTA only if the Americans raised the issue.
"We are not going to be the cheerleaders of NAFTA in the United States. That's not our role," he told reporters. Frei is to visit Washington from Feb. 24.

Insulza was sceptical about statements by U.S. Commerce Secretary-designate Mickey Kantor that Chile might be able to join the United States, Mexico and Canada in the North American Free Trade Agreement this year.
"We've heard that many times before. We're going to wait patiently," Insulza said.

Former U.S. president George Bush and later Clinton promised to bring Chile, which has Latin America's strongest economy, into NAFTA. But Congress balked at granting "fast-track" powers that would allow U.S. officials to negotiate a treaty.
Insulza hinted he was sceptical that Congress would make fast-track a priority, saying ''I'm sure the American legislative agenda has a great number of issues on it."'

Chile, which last year had its 13th straight year of growth, was supposed to become a full member of NAFTA by mid- 1996 under a timetable set by Clinton at the Summit of the Americas in Miami in 1994.
Chile signed a NAFTA-style free trade agreement with Canada last year, but substantive talks to become NAFTA's fourth partner will have to wait until fast track passes, Chilean officials say.
